minutes.headline: Losing a quorum member forces the 390 Howard Street wetlands case to be renotified, possibly refiled
minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission held hearings and administrative reviews for several wetlands filings, approving a negative determination for a restaurant patio, a continuance for another patio project, ratification of a landscaping determination, and a certificate of compliance for restored plantings. Members marked departing commissioner Jeff Viviano's final meeting and welcomed a new commissioner, discussed how to handle the 390 Howard Street case after losing a quorum, and voted to renew MACC membership dues at an amended figure.

what_happened.line: Losing a quorum member forced the 390 Howard Street wetlands applicant to renotify abutters, and possibly refile the case, before it can be decided.
The commission approved a negative determination allowing a stone patio replacement at 5 Electric Ave, with erosion-control and posting conditions.
A request for determination at 67 Island Road was continued to July 9, and a certificate of compliance was approved for restored plantings at 564 Page Street.
Members raised the annual MACC membership dues payment, amending the motion twice to add handbook and administrator access before final approval.
The July meeting schedule was shifted from the 2nd and 16th to the 9th and 23rd to ensure a quorum for the continued hearing.

why_it_matters: A wetlands applicant at 390 Howard Street may face renotification or a full refiling because the board lost a quorum member, which can add delay and possibly cost depending on the chair's decision.
Conditions attached to the 5 Electric Ave patio approval and the closeout at 564 Page Street show how the commission manages construction near protected wetland buffers.
The rescheduled July meeting dates matter for anyone tracking the continued 67 Island Road case or planning to attend or comment.
